exposure: Traditional Chinese medicine analgesic and delivery-aiding patches in combination with doula-assisted childbirth
outcome: Duration of labor (first, second, and total labor times)
Pain intensity (NRS scores during latent and active phases)
Postpartum hemorrhage (at 2 hours and 24 hours after delivery)
cohort: The study included 240 puerperae (120 in the control group and 120 in the observation group) undergoing childbirth at Haian Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
finding: The application of traditional Chinese medicine analgesics and delivery-aiding patches in doula-assisted childbirth significantly reduced the cesarean section rate, shortened labor durations, alleviated labor pain, and reduced postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was significantly lower (12.50%) in the group utilizing traditional Chinese medicine patches and doula assistance compared to the control group (25.83%).
